summary: Iteration 4 testing — Photo Reactions (like + bookmark). Backend: 9/9 new iter4 pytest cases pass covering POST /api/photos/{id}/reactions (auth-required, invalid type→400, unknown photo→404, like toggle, like+bookmark independence, my_liked/my_bookmarked reflection), GET /api/hotels/{id}/photos with counts + my_* flags (unauth defaults false), ordering (likes DESC, bookmark DESC, created_at DESC with 3-photo seed + tiebreak on same counts), GET /api/photos/bookmarks (auth-required, reverse chronological, includes url). Full regression: 67/68 pass — 1 PRE-EXISTING xdist race in test_travelo_iter2.py::TestEmails::test_emails_mine_lists_mocked (unrelated to iter4; passes in serial with -n 0; reason: xdist loadscope splits TestBundleBookings and TestEmails onto different workers with separate seeded_session users). Frontend PhotoWall on /hotels/htl_01: unauth click → 'Sign in to react to photos' toast (no count change); authed click → orange like button + bg-white bookmark button, counts increment (+1) and toggle back (-1), reactions independent; 'Top shot' badge appears on top-ranked tile after reactions; lightbox opens on tile click, lightbox-like-btn/lightbox-bookmark-btn present with counts that sync with grid tiles on toggle. Screenshot captured showing filled bookmark (count 1) in lightbox.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Address the pre-existing xdist race in TestEmails (not an iter4 regression — passes in serial).
Consider server.py refactor into modules (recurring since iter2, now 1112 lines with reactions added).

Sort in list_hotel_photos is done client-side over up to 200 rows and does THREE .sort() calls (lines 942/944/946) — only the last one is effective; the first two are dead code. Trim to a single sort for clarity.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to 1112 lines — split into routers (routers/photos.py, routers/reactions.py, routers/wishlist.py, etc.). This has been recommended across iter2/iter3/iter4.

list_hotel_photos has THREE consecutive rows.sort() calls (lines 942, 944, 946) as a workaround; only the last is effective. Please delete lines 942-945 to keep just the correct sort by (like_count, bookmark_count, created_at) desc.
POST /api/photos/{photo_id}/reactions has no rate limiting — a malicious user could rapid-toggle to hammer the DB. Consider a small per-user per-photo cooldown or IP-level limit.

GET /api/photos/bookmarks returns up to 200 photos but does not de-duplicate hotel_photos rows if a photo_id points to a deleted photo (find({photo_id: {$in: []}}) still ok, but if photo was deleted after bookmark, the bookmark reaction is orphaned and silently dropped from the list). Consider surfacing orphaned bookmarks or cleaning them up.

photo_reactions has no compound unique index on (photo_id, user_id, reaction_type) — a race could theoretically insert duplicate reactions if two toggle requests arrive concurrently. Consider `db.photo_reactions.create_index([('photo_id', 1), ('user_id', 1), ('reaction_type', 1)], unique=True)` at startup.

get_current_user Optional dependency is used by list_hotel_photos so my_liked/my_bookmarked reflect the caller — good. But it depends on cookie OR bearer; ensure both are tested in production (bearer path is covered here, cookie path relies on frontend axios withCredentials which was already working in iter3).

Object storage still uses local FS fallback (documented) — files persist under /app/backend/uploads and are lost on redeploy. Not an iter4 change but worth calling out that reactions target photos whose file bytes may vanish.

rca_of_the_issue: test_travelo_iter2.py::TestEmails::test_emails_mine_lists_mocked FAILURE RCA: pytest.ini enforces `-n 2 --dist loadscope` — with loadscope, each TEST CLASS is a scope group and can be assigned to a different worker. TestBundleBookings runs on gw0 and generates the mocked email (via /api/payments/verify) for gw0's seeded_session user_id. TestEmails runs on gw1 with a DIFFERENT seeded_session user_id (session-scoped fixtures are per-worker under xdist). So gw1's /api/emails/mine call returns [] because that user never created a booking. MITIGATION: Move the email-list assertion into TestBundleBookings class so it always runs on the same worker as its dependency, OR query mongo_db.emails directly by TestBundleBookings.bundle_booking_id (which is a class attribute that would only work within same worker anyway — so the cleanest fix is class consolidation). Verified: `pytest backend/tests/test_travelo_iter2.py -n 0` → 12/12 pass.
